article_text:
In DC Studios ‘ Clayface , Tom Rhys Harries’ titular shape-shifting Batman villain takes multiple forms, including a surprising familiar face.

Following murmurs of a cameo, director James Watkins confirmed that Aaron Paul makes a brief appearance in the DCU movie as Matt’s (Harries) father, who raised him in the slums of Gotham City.

“He has a real brief Easter egg kind of moment,” Watkins told Entertainment Weekly .

Related Stories

‘Clayface’ Review: DCU Molds Batman Villain’s Origin Story Into Fun, Scary Body Horror

‘Clayface’ Trailer: DC Studios’ Batman Bad Guy Gets His Close-Up

While flashbacks of Paul as Matt’s father were ultimately cut from the film, the Breaking Bad alum makes a quick appearance in the action-packed Club Vesuvius scene, in which Matt shape-shifts into multiple people to take on Szabo’s (David Dencik) goons before taking has dad’s form to kill Jimmy “One Nut” (Enzo Squillino Jr.), the gangster who took his father’s life years before.

Watch on Deadline

“In terms of trying to figure out the character, it was, How much is Matt defined by his past and how much is he an everyman?” the director explained. “At one point, we were looking at it and thinking, Is it the ‘sins of the father’?”

Watkins continued, “But actually, as we worked on the script, I thought that notion of revenge was more universal and more relatable to all of us. It doesn’t matter whether you’re carrying a trauma or any of that. If we’re slighted, we carry this sense of being wronged and we all want to do something, but generally in life we can’t do anything about it and we’re powerless.”

Now playing in theaters, Clayface stars Harries as rising actor Matt Hagen, who suffers gruesome wounds after the brutal mafioso Szabo (Dencik) cuts up his face, resulting in the downfall of his career. But when he discovers the groundbreaking nanotech research of Dr. Caitlyn Corr (Naomi Ackie), Matt convinces her to restore his face to its former glory, only to result in terrifying side effects and a bloody quest for revenge.

title_original: Torinodanza, il ritorno all’intimità di Damien Jalet e gli anni Ottanta di Kyle Abraham
editorial_title_zh: Torinodanza，达米安·雅莱重回亲密感，凯尔·亚伯拉罕致敬八十年代
editorial_excerpt_zh: Torinodanza 艺术节以达米安·雅莱的《Thrice》和凯尔·亚伯拉罕的《Cassette Vol. 1》闭幕，这两部全国首演作品融合了自然元素、黑人音乐与八十年代文化。本文源自……

"https://www.exibart.com/tag/torinodanza/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "达米安·雅莱的《Thrice》", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "相较于他那些以宏大布景影响并放大肢体动作的惊艳创作，法比裔编导达米安·雅莱的演出《Thrice》标志着他回归到更为亲密的维度。《Thrice》（在 Torinodanza 艺术节上进行全国首演）让我们得以进入一个与我们更为贴近的世界。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "空气、石头、水，构成了这三部独立作品标题所指的三个自然元素：《Gusts》、《Médusés》、《Brise-lames》。第一部在挪威爵士萨克斯风手本迪克·吉斯克（Bendik Giske）的现场音乐伴奏下，探索了呼吸与空中运动。第二部灵感取自美杜莎的神话以及她那能使生命物质化为石头的凝视力量。第三部则更为复杂，将躯体带入一个充满深厚情感的水下景观中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "雅莱的灵感源自墨西哥作家奥克塔维奥·帕斯（Octavio Paz）的一首诗，其诗句唤起了上述的种种元素。在《Gusts》中，空气通过萨克斯风的声音被唤起，起初是吹气声，随后是三位身着红衣的舞者躯体所放大的和声或不和谐音阶。他们躬身于地毯之上，以螺旋形动作、旋转、摇晃等宛如阵风般的姿态追逐着那团声音的漩涡。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/2-Médusés-Brise-lames-Damien-Jalet_Thrice-©Rahi-Rezvani.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Médusés, Brise-lames, Damien Jalet, Thrice © Rahi Rezvani", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Médusés》借用了三位表演者带有幽默感的无声电影姿态，他们在涂满白粉的边缘区域内互相穿梭。在触摸、抬起和挪动彼此的过程中，他们轮流定格在突如其来的雕塑般手势中；接着一人瞬间解冻，而将其唤醒的另一人则化为石雕；如此这般形成连锁反应，仿佛在传递一种具传染性的病毒。在三位身穿黑衣的男子之后，登场的是一队身着白色条纹服装的女舞者，她们起初宛如大理石块般静止，随后在 Winter Family 的打击乐音效与加布里埃莱·米拉奇（Gabriele Miracle）的节奏序列中，释放出充满活力、流畅而飘逸的舞蹈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/3-Médusés-Brise-lames-Damien-Jalet_Thrice-©Rahi-Rezvani.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Médusés, Brise-lames, Damien Jalet, Thrice © Rahi Rezvani", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "九名舞者身着带有浅蓝色条纹的浅灰色服装，从舞台后方正面步步逼近，如海藻般以多种形态摇曳，将我们引入了《Brise-lames》的海洋维度（该标题意指保护海岸免受海浪暴力侵袭的防波堤）。在法比安娜·佩奇奥利（Fabiana Peccioli）的灯光以及日本钢琴家中野公挥（Koki Nakano）现场演奏的音乐的配合下，雅莱与视觉艺术家 JR 合作创作的这支富有诗意、充满张力的编舞，不仅是一首具有极高构图美的作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当这些躯体展现出对海浪威力的抗拒、向各个方向运动犹如形成、碎裂、传播、蓄力又折返的海浪时，它便具有了政治与社会的维度；而在最终精疲力竭的尾声中，它们在地面聚拢，化作了一艘迷失在茫茫大海中的难民船。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/4-Brise-lames-Nagelhus-Schia-Productions_Damien-Jalet_Thrice_carchlabyrinth.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Brise-lames, Nagelhus Schia Productions, Damien Jalet, Thrice, (c) archlabyrinth", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "将影像投射在正面墙上，摄像机从高处进行实时变焦，其形态逐渐揭示并聚焦在成堆人群的中心——一名女子。或许是唯一的幸存者。她昂起头凝视着我们，向我们质问。这是对我们冷漠态度的一次当头棒喝。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "凯尔·亚伯拉罕的《Cassette Vol. 1》", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "舞台是一面带有几何粉饰的大墙。墙前摆放着灰色的橱窗模特、一部公用电话，以及几台悬挂在不同高度的旧电视机，上面循环播放着广告、情景喜剧、美国面孔与活动的画面。一名男子在地上放下一台便携式立体声磁带录音机，按下播放键，随即开启了一场色彩斑斓、妙趣横生、充满活力的演出。演出伴随着大量的音乐，身穿复古运动服、头顶蓬松假发的舞者们不断地登场与退场。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/6-AIM-By-Kyle-Abraham_Christopher-Dugga.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "AIM, Kyle Abraham, Christopher Duggan", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "美国编导凯尔·亚伯拉罕及其舞团 AIM 的《Cassette Vol. 1》（在 Torinodanza 艺术节上进行全国首演），对于经历过那个音乐时代（八十年代至九十年代）的人来说，可以被视为一次令人欣喜的怀旧操作，让人不禁感慨“我们曾如此年轻”。而对于其他世代、只熟悉那些已融入集体想象中的标志性歌曲的观众来说，这场演出则可以被体验为一种激励身体离开座位的动力，那种让人跺脚并渴望起舞的沉浸感。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对于最挑剔的舞蹈鉴赏家而言，它展现了后现代主义的一小片截面，其中包含了对崔莎·布朗（Trisha Brown）（以《Set and reset》中迅捷、灵动且流畅的动作为开端）或露辛达·柴尔兹（Lucinda Childs）的致敬，以及释放技巧（release technique）——这种风格建立在释放肌肉紧张与身体自然运用之上。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "它也向我们讲述了一些关于非裔美国人社群的事情，以及那个时代社会中赋予其特征的多元性。其中融入了凯尔·亚伯拉罕的青春记忆——他原籍匹兹堡，出生于七十年代末——在流行乐、R&B、新浪潮（New Wave）、锐舞、黑人音乐、录音带、MTV 节目、录像带以及后来的俱乐部文化和街头舞蹈的伴随下长大。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/7-AIM-By-Kyle-Abraham_Christopher-Duggan.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "AIM, Kyle Abraham, Christopher Duggan", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这场艺术与生存的混融中，表演者的肢体动作在流畅的手势、步伐、独舞与群舞序列之间穿梭，兼具古典、现代、极简与释放（release）技巧的杂糅。演出伴随着一盘磁带（作为演出标题的怀旧物品）中的精选曲目，这些音乐从普林斯（Prince）的《Let's Work》到香蕉女郎（Bananarama）的《Venus》，再到比利·偶像（Billy Idol）、手镯乐队（The Bangles）、指针姐妹（The Pointer Sisters）的《Jump (For My Love)》等等。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，无论音乐是优美抒情还是欢快铿锵，整场编舞在不同的曲目中流淌时，仅带着些许变化，显得单调而重复。最后，为了给舞台增添更多色彩，在舞蹈持续进行的同时，玩具、玩偶和库什球（Koosh，还记得用来缓解压力的个性化海绵球吗？）被抛向地面。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
Il festival Torinodanza chiude con altri due coreografi internazionali: Damien Jalet e Kyle Abraham.

Thrice di Damien Jalet

Rispetto alle sue sorprendenti creazioni fatte di scenografie monumentali che influenzano e amplificano il movimento, lo spettacolo Thrice di Damien Jalet rappresenta un ritorno a una dimensione più intima del coreografo franco-belga. Thrice (prima nazionale al Festival Torinodanza) ci fa entrare in un mondo a noi più prossimo.

Aria, pietra, acqua, sono i tre elementi della natura che danno il titolo ai tre singoli pezzi: Gusts , Médusés , Brise-lames. Il primo, accompagnato dalla musica dal vivo del sassofonista jazz norvegese Bendik Giske, esplora il respiro e il movimento aereo. Il secondo si ispira al mito di Medusa e alla capacità del suo sguardo di pietrificare la materia viva. Il terzo, più complesso, trasporta i corpi in un paesaggio subacqueo e profondamente emotivo.

A ispirare Jalet è stata una poesia dello scrittore messicano Octavio Paz i cui versi richiamano gli elementi evocati. In Gusts l’aria è evocata dal suono del sax inizialmente soffiato, poi in progressioni armoniche o dissonanti che i corpi dei tre danzatori dai costumi rossi, amplificano. Stando a terra dentro un tappeto, inseguono quel vortice sonoro con movimenti a spirale, roteazioni, ondeggiamenti simili a raffiche di vento.

Médusés gioca con le umoristiche posture da cinema muto di tre performer intenti a spostarsi reciprocamente da un punto all’altro del perimetro imbrattato di polvere bianca. Nell’atto di toccarsi, sollevarsi e rimuovere, si bloccano a turno in improvvisi gesti scultorei; immediatamente uno si sblocca e l’altro che lo ha rianimato si pietrifica; e via così, a catena, come a trasmettersi un virus contagioso. Ai tre uomini in costume nero, subentra un terzetto di donne con vesti di strisce bianche, posizionate inizialmente come blocchi marmorei, poi liberatesi in una danza energica, fluida e fluttuante al suono percussivo della musica di Winter Family e della sequenza ritmica di Gabriele Miracle .

Il costume grigio chiaro con striature azzurre indossato dai nove danzatori che avanzano frontalmente dal fondo ondeggiando in molte forme come alghe, ci immette nella dimensione marina di Brise-lames (titolo riferito ai frangiflutti che proteggono dalla violenza delle onde). Complici le luci di Fabiana Peccioli e le musiche del pianista giapponese Koki Nakano eseguite dal vivo, la poetica, vibrante, coreografia di Jalet creata in collaborazione con l’artista visivo JR, non è solamente un brano di grande bellezza compositiva.

Assume una dimensione politica, sociale, quando, manifestando resistenza alla potenza dei flutti, quei corpi, mossi in tutte le direzioni come onde che si formano, si infrangono, si propagano, che acquistano forza e ritornano, nel finale che li trova ormai esausti, si raggruppano a terra formando un barcone di naufraghi persi nella vastità del mare.

Proiettando l’immagine sulla parete frontale, la forma lo svela il progressivo zoomare in diretta di una telecamera dall’alto, focalizzando, al centro del gruppo ammassato, una donna. Forse l’unica sopravvissuta. Con la testa alzata ci guarda intensamente, interpellandoci. Un pugno allo stomaco alla nostra indifferenza.

Cassette Vol. 1 di Kyle Abraham

La scena è un grande muro con stucchi geometrici. Davanti ad esso dei grigi manichini da vetrina, un telefono pubblico, dei vecchi televisori sospesi a varie altezze dove scorrono immagini di pubblicità, di sit-com, di volti ed eventi americani. Un uomo con uno stereo portatile a terra inserisce un musicassette, preme il tasto, e prende il via un colorato, giocoso, spumeggiante spettacolo con tanta musica, caratterizzato da continue entrate e uscite di danzatori dalle tute ginniche vintage e vaporosi parrucconi in testa.

Cassette Vol. 1 del coreografo statunitense Kyle Abraham con la sua compagnia AIM (prima nazionale al Festival Torinodanza), lo si può guardare come un’operazione felicemente nostalgica per chi ha vissuto un’epoca di musica, gli anni Ottanta-Novanta, che fa dire “come eravamo”. Per chi, invece, di altra generazione, conosce quelle canzoni iconiche entrate nell’immaginario collettivo, lo spettacolo lo si può vivere come uno stimolo a far muovere il corpo dalla poltrona, quella sensazione coinvolgente che fa battere il piede invogliando a ballare.

Ai più attenti conoscitori della danza rappresenta un piccolo spaccato della postmodern, con citazioni a Trisha Brown (l’inizio di Set and reset coi movimenti rapidi, guizzanti e fluidi), o a Lucinda Childs, e alla tecnica release – quello stile fondato sul rilascio delle tensioni muscolari e sull’uso naturale del corpo -.

Ci dice anche qualcosa della comunità afroamericana, delle diversità che la contraddistinguevano nella società dell’epoca. C’è la giovinezza di Kyle Abraham – originario di Pittsburg, nato a fine anni Settanta – cresciuto coi suoni del pop, del R&B, del New Wave, dei rave, della black-music, delle videocassette, della trasmissione MTV, dei videoclip, e via via del club culture, della street-dance.

In questo mix artistico ed esistenziale, il movimento dei performer, tra morbidezze di gesti, camminate, assoli e sequenze di gruppo, è un ibrido di tecnica classica, modern, minimalismo e release , eseguito su una compilation di brani contenuti in una musicassetta (oggetto d’antan che dà il titolo allo spettacolo) che spaziano da Let’s Work di Prince a Venus di Bananarama, da Billy Idol a The Bangles a The Pointer Sisters di Jump (For My Love) e molti altri.

La coreografia, con appena qualche variante, scorre però monotona e ripetitiva sulle diverse canzoni, che siano melodiche, o più allegre e ritmate. In ultimo, a colorare ulteriormente la scena, mentre si continua a ballare, vengono lanciate a terra giocattoli, pupazzetti e palline Koosh (ricordate le bilie di spugna personalizzate per alleviare lo stress?).

Insomma, spettacolo gradevole, ironico e spensierato – tra l’altro di appena 55 minuti -, ma non ci dice qualcosa in più degli aspetti culturali e sociali di quel periodo, riferimenti significativi che, se approfonditi o solo accennati, avrebbero potuto contestualizzare maggiormente la messa in scena, oltre alla scrittura coreografica, e arricchirla di contenuto.

“Cassette Vol. 1”, dopo Torinodanza ha proseguito la tournée alla Triennale di Milano, al Teatro Valli di Reggio Emilia per il Festival Aperto, e al Teatro Grande di Brescia.

Le Joueur

Un film de Elie Wajeman

Avec Pio Marmai, William Lebghil, Sarah Le Picard, Suzy Bemba, avec la participation de Hippolyte Girardot

Genre : Thriller psychologique

Durée : 1h43

Metteur en scène de théâtre et joueur pathologique, Ivan Katz brûle sa vie dans les jeux d'argent. Une nuit, il joue et perd les fonds destinés à la production de sa nouvelle pièce : Platonov, de Tchekhov. Pour se refaire, il n’a d’autre choix que d’entrer dans les parties clandestines de poker. Tout en répétant le jour, Ivan plonge dans l’univers vertigineux et dangereux du jeu la nuit…

Un film réalisé par Élie Wajeman

article_text:
Greta Gerwig is inviting audiences to enter the epic realm of Narnia with “The Magician’s Nephew,” for which the first trailer was unveiled on Tuesday.

Based on the classic C.S. Lewis children’s book series “The Chronicles of Narnia,” the story follows two children, Digory and Polly, who are the first to discover the “Wood between the Worlds,” otherwise known as Narnia. Scored to Led Zeppelin’s “Stairway to Heaven,” the cosmic trailer opens with an unnamed narrator opining that “sometimes one story is the beginning of all the others” before Daniel Craig’s Andrew Ketterley — the titular magician — gives the youngsters a magical ring that transports them to various fantastical lands. The kids are spellbound as they come into contact with mythical creatures, beings and beasts including Emma Mackey’s Jadis, the future White Witch and last Queen of Charn, and Fledge, a talking horse who is capable of flight.

Related Stories

Kenan Thompson Says Shane Gillis 'SNL' Monologue Backlash 'Overshadowed' the Episode and 'We Would Have to Have a Real Chat' If He Hosts Again

“Have you ever seen a world born?” the narrator asks before a glimpse of Aslan, the mythical lion voiced by the one and only Meryl Streep, singing Narnia to life.

Popular on Variety

Ahead of the trailer’s launch, Netflix hosted a preview event for press and social media influencers at New York’s AMC Lincoln Square. Attendees were treated at 9 a.m. to colorful cocktails, popcorn, boxed candy and tray-passed hors d’oeuvres. Gerwig was interviewed by Stephen Colbert, who asked the Oscar-nominated director about adapting the beloved Lewis novel, finding young actors David McKenna and Beatrice Campbell to anchor the movie, and populating the mystical world with stars such as Streep, Craig, Carey Mulligan and Ciarán Hinds.

“I don’t remember a time I didn’t know the books,” Gerwig said. “I wouldn’t be who I am without these books.”

Gerwig said she found herself in Netflix’s orbit around the time the streamer was releasing her husband Noah Baumbach’s 2019’s film “Marriage Story.” A year prior, Netflix had acquired the rights to “The Chronicles of Narnia” property.

“I made a beeline for Ted Sarandos at a cocktail party and said, ‘I really think you should start with ‘The Magician’s Nephew,’” said Gerwig, who joked that she continued to ramble about her thoughts to the CEO. “About 20 minutes later he said, ‘Do you want to write it?’ At that point, I had only made ‘Lady Bird’ and ‘Little Women.’ I hadn’t done ‘Barbie’ yet.”

Although Lewis’ seven-book series began with 1950’s “The Lion the Witch and the Wardrobe,” the author retroactively noted he wanted readers to start with “The Magician’s Nephew,” which was published in 1955 and serves as a prequel to the otherworldly story. His novels were first adapted into a BBC miniseries, which ran from 1988 to 1990, and later into three films — 2005’s “The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe,” 2008’s “Prince Caspian” and 2010’s “The Voyage of the Dawn Treader” — by Disney and 20th Century.

“The Magician’s Nephew” is Gerwig’s first feature since 2023’s acclaimed box office smash “Barbie,” and the adaptation is notable as Netflix’s first movie to receive a global theatrical release. The film will opens in cinemas on Feb. 12, 2027 before landing on Netflix on April 2.

“I told Ted I only know how to make movies for the big screen,” Gerwig said. “‘He said, ‘Make the movie for the biggest screen and trust the process.’”

Gerwig spoke about casting McKenna and Campbell, having scoured through thousands of taped auditions over the course of several months, and recalled the instant she knew she found her leads.

“We were doing a screen test, which is intimidating for any actor, and there was a moment when Bea sniffled and David gestured off camera to get her a Kleenex. I thought, ‘Oh, these kids are already taking care of each other.’”

If McKenna and Campbell were intimidated to work with stars like Craig and Mulligan, they didn’t show it. Gerwig brought up a funny moment from set before the cameras started to roll. “We were doing rehearsals, and Daniel Craig said to the kids, ‘I’m a bit nervous,’ just to be nice,” Gerwig said. “And they said, ‘Don’t worry, Greta is really nice. You’ll be fine!’”

Gerwig has described “Narnia” as “a world made out of music,” so finding the right songs — including “Stairway to Heaven” — was central in bringing the story to life. Led Zeppelin has always been reluctant to license their discography for film or television. So Gerwig wrote to the band’s vocalist Robert Plant and guitarist Jimmy Page and showed them an early cut of the film to convince them to let her use their rock anthem for the big screen.

“It’s an epic song, and narratively, about a spiritual journey, a path of fake idols and wrong roads you can go down. It made sense to introduce the world,” Gerwig said. “I was so moved that they allowed me to use this song. They saw the heart and story of the film.”

Gerwig wants audience to experience a similar sentiment when they finally get to see “The Magician’s Nephew.”

“I hope they laugh. I hope they cry. I hope they feel like they’ve been on an adventure,” Gerwig said. “I hope when they leave the theater, they want to make something, a song or a cake or a song or a painting. Making something is an act of hope.”

article_text:
La plataforma confirmó una nueva producción de acción real ambientada en la década de 1950. Será una precuela de la historia original, estará creada por los hermanos Duffer y Kate Trefry y contará con Joe Wright como director de sus primeros episodios.

El universo de Stranger Things seguirá expandiéndose. En el marco de una nueva celebración del Día de Stranger Things , Netflix anunció oficialmente Otros Mundos: Una Aventura de Stranger Things , una nueva serie derivada de acción real que funcionará como precuela de la exitosa ficción creada por Matt y Ross Duffer. La producción tiene previsto su estreno en 2028 y llevará a los espectadores a una época anterior a los acontecimientos de la historia original.

Ambientada en la década de 1950, la nueva ficción se desarrollará antes de los acontecimientos de Stranger Things y de la obra teatral Stranger Things: The First Shadow . De esta manera, la plataforma buscará explorar una etapa inédita de la mitología de la franquicia, con nuevos personajes, héroes, villanos y misterios, aunque manteniendo el espíritu de terror, aventura y ciencia ficción que convirtió a la serie en un fenómeno mundial.

Uno de los nombres destacados del proyecto es Joe Wright, reconocido director de películas como Orgullo y prejuicio , Expiación, deseo y pecado y Las horas más oscuras . El cineasta estará a cargo de la dirección de los tres primeros episodios de la producción, cuyo rodaje se llevará adelante en Nuevo México.

Quiénes están detrás de la nueva serie de Stranger Things

Otros Mundos: Una Aventura de Stranger Things fue creada por los hermanos Duffer junto a Kate Trefry, quien también se desempeñará como showrunner, guionista y productora ejecutiva. Trefry cuenta con una extensa trayectoria dentro de Stranger Things , donde trabajó como guionista, además de ser la dramaturga responsable de Stranger Things: The First Shadow , la exitosa obra teatral ambientada en el universo de la franquicia.

Por su parte, Matt y Ross Duffer participarán como productores ejecutivos a través de su compañía Upside Down Pictures. Shawn Levy también regresará como productor ejecutivo en representación de 21 Laps Entertainment, productora que participa en el desarrollo de esta nueva historia.

El equipo de producción ejecutiva se completa con Paul Dichter, Shelley Meals, Andrea Sperling y Pavlina Hatoupis.

Qué dijeron sus creadores sobre Otros Mundos

El anuncio estuvo acompañado por declaraciones de los principales responsables del proyecto. Jinny Howe, directora de Series de Ficción de Netflix para Estados Unidos y Canadá, destacó la posibilidad de seguir ampliando una franquicia que mantiene una enorme conexión con sus seguidores.

“ Stranger Things siempre les ha pertenecido a los fans, y su pasión la convirtió en un fenómeno mundial. Hoy, en el Día de Stranger Things, es un honor volver a colaborar con Matt y Ross Duffer y Kate Trefry para ofrecerles a los fans una nueva dimensión de este universo en la que puedan adentrarse”, expresó.

Además, adelantó que la producción trasladará al público a los años 50, con nuevos protagonistas y todo el misterio y la espectacularidad de la serie original.

Los hermanos Duffer también manifestaron su entusiasmo por concretar una idea que llevan desarrollando desde hace varios años.

“Llevamos muchos años soñando con Otros Mundos: Una Aventura de Stranger Things , y verla hacerse realidad es tan surrealista como emocionante. Estamos muy agradecidos con nuestro increíble equipo de colaboradores: nuestra showrunner, Kate Trefry, quien nos acompaña desde la segunda temporada y escribió Stranger Things: The First Shadow ; y nuestro director, Joe Wright, un artista brillante cuyo trabajo admiramos desde hace mucho tiempo”, señalaron.

Por su parte, Kate Trefry aseguró que será un privilegio ponerse al frente de este nuevo capítulo de la franquicia y anticipó una historia que volverá a combinar terror, asombro y misterio, aunque con una identidad propia.

Shawn Levy, productor ejecutivo de 21 Laps Entertainment, también destacó que la serie presentará una nueva aventura con personajes y una mitología diferentes, pero conservará la esencia de la producción original.

El fenómeno Stranger Things: una franquicia que sigue creciendo

Desde su estreno en 2016, Stranger Things se convirtió en uno de los mayores éxitos de la historia de Netflix. La ficción acumuló más de 1.200 millones de visualizaciones entre sus primeras cuatro temporadas y construyó un fenómeno cultural que trascendió la pantalla.

La quinta y última temporada consiguió la semana de estreno más exitosa de Netflix para una serie de habla inglesa. Además, volvió a impulsar las temporadas anteriores al Top 10 global de la plataforma durante ocho semanas y estableció un récord de visualizaciones el día de Año Nuevo.

El impacto de la producción también se reflejó en la música, con canciones como “Running Up That Hill”, de Kate Bush, que regresaron a las listas de éxitos gracias a su aparición en la ficción. A lo largo de su recorrido, la serie recibió más de 70 premios internacionales, incluidos varios Emmy y un reconocimiento del Sindicato de Actores (SAG) al mejor elenco de una serie dramática.

La franquicia también se expandió con la serie animada Stranger Things: Tales From ’85 , la obra teatral Stranger Things: The First Shadow , libros, experiencias inmersivas y distintas propuestas vinculadas al universo de Hawkins.

Con Otros Mundos: Una Aventura de Stranger Things , Netflix apuesta nuevamente por una de sus propiedades más exitosas y abre la puerta a descubrir una etapa completamente diferente de su mitología.

article_text:
Jenny Wu looks at the acrobatics required when successful writers – from Berger to Émile Zola – seek to hold on to a connection with the working class

When Étienne Lantier, hero of Émile Zola’s 1885 novel Germinal , first sees the coalmine in which he is to work and the oppressive conditions of which will later cause him to lead a strike, he observes that ‘the pit could swallow people in mouthfuls’. A four-deck elevator appears from below filled with tubs of coal; these are removed and replaced with empty containers, into which the miners themselves then climb. ‘An order would issue from the loudhailer in the form of a muffled, unintelligible bellow,’ Zola writes, ‘while the signal-rope was pulled four times to indicate a “meat load”, warning those below that a cargo of human flesh was on its way down.’

Imagine: February 1884, Zola in his mid-forties drops into a pit in Anzin, a small mining town near Valenciennes, in Northern France, where 10,000 workers are on strike, to conduct research for this, the 13th book in his 20-volume Rougon-Macquart cycle (1871–93). Frederick Brown, who begins his 1995 biography Zola: A Life by characterising the writer’s father as a ‘portly bourgeois’, remarks on Zola’s own ‘stout’ physiognomy and supposes that having a ‘forty-five-inch waist must have been especially inconvenient underground’.

John Berger agrees: Zola must have been uncomfortable. In the late English art critic and novelist’s rarely screened BBC documentary Germinal (1973), which was brought out in August for a Film Comment programme in New York commemorating his centenary, Berger, an avowed Marxist, conducts his own reconnaissance, descending into a pit in Creswell, on the Nottinghamshire–Derbyshire border. His images are restrained compared to Zola’s prose; nonetheless, they convey the mine’s atmosphere. Berger enters wearing a hard hat, his brow furrowed, observing in voiceover that the air underground is “hot and silted with coal dust” and that as you go down “there’s less and less space for your body”.

Zola must have been self-conscious, Berger surmises. Despite the French author’s “working-class sympathies” – an extension of his support for the Republic and its ideals of social progress – by the time he was drafting Germinal , “Zola was rich and successful. He wrote his novels in a villa near Paris.” The villa was, as Berger’s latest biographer, Tom Overton, writes when describing the documentary, ‘closer to the home of a mine owner than one of a worker’, a fact that must have ‘disturbed’ Zola, given as he was to rail against bourgeois sensibilities on the page. But Berger, too, seems anxious in the pit. Not long after those few establishing shots, he retires to the village bar to ruminate. Now confidently addressing the camera, having put on a cosy sweater, he implies that the surest way to close the gap between the writer and the miner is for the former to become the latter – or at least to visit the pits “400 or 4,000 times” more.

Despite obvious differences, Zola’s and Berger’s lives mirrored each other in several significant respects. Both wrote for periodicals: Zola as a political journalist in his early thirties, reporting on the French National Assembly for outlets like La Cloche and Le Sémaphore de Marseille , Berger as a cultural critic for The New Statesman , The Nation and Art News and Review (as ArtReview was once called). Both kept homes in the French countryside: Zola in Médan, Berger in Quincy. Both benefitted materially from their interest in the struggles of socially and economically disenfranchised groups. Berger’s work on Germinal followed on the heels of his Booker Prize-winning novel G. (1972). Within three weeks of his declaring that he would share his prize money with the British Black Panthers, G. sold 1,200 copies. The trials of Zola’s working-class heroine Gervaise Macquart, who suffers from debt, alcoholism and domestic violence in the seventh installment of the Rougon-Macquart series, L’Assommoir (1877), earned him around £3,000 per year in royalties, and leftists rebuked the profitable book for, as Victor Hugo reportedly said, ‘reveal[ing], as if delightedly, the hideous sores of misery and the abjection to which the poor man finds himself reduced’. Zola redeemed himself only when he revisited the subject of the working class in Germinal , which was nothing short of what Brown called a ‘proletarian gospel story’.

An unspoken desire for a similar sort of literary redemption permeates the remainder of Berger’s televised homage to Zola, during which the twentieth-century writer recites from the nineteenth-century novel a passage about the vengeance of the working class, which promises to split the earth from within, as if language might hasten the arrival of this revolution or weave both storyteller and listener into their ranks. The inhabitants of Creswell go about their day – working, rehearsing a musical, playing bingo in the village clubhouse – and the writer continues to wring his hands.

article_text:
Gefälschte Kunstwerke für britische Künstler-Visa, Trump-Spott von The Secret Handshake, und die Frieze Abu Dhabi steht trotz geopolitischer Spannungen in den Startlöchern: Das ist unsere Medienschau am Freitag

Kunstbetrieb

Die BBC berichtet über Unternehmen, die wohlhabenden Migranten gegen hohe Summen gefälschte Künstlerportfolios für britische Global-Talent-Visa anbieten. Ein Undercover-Reporter sei bei einer Londoner Beratungsfirma auf ein Komplettpaket für rund 100.000 Pfund gestoßen: Die Firma habe angeboten, in China Kunstwerke produzieren zu lassen, Ausstellungen und Medienberichte zu arrangieren und sogar einen Forbes-gesponserten Kunstpreis zu vermitteln. Ein Mitarbeiter habe versichert: "Es spielt keine Rolle, ob Sie Künstler sind" – die Firma liefere die Werke gleich mit. Der britische Innenminister lasse nun die Visa zweier Nigerianer widerrufen, die ihre Anträge mit gefälschten Rezensionen und Kunstwerken gestützt hätten. Die nigerianische Kunstkritikerin Molara Wood habe sich gegen die missbräuchliche Verwendung ihres Namens gewehrt: "Es gibt ein echtes Problem damit, dass gefälschte Artikel unter den Namen angesehener Kulturjournalisten auf Nachrichtenseiten platziert werden." Die BBC-Recherche hat eine Untersuchung des Innenministeriums ausgelöst.

In Chicago hält sich hartnäckig das Gerücht, ein Mann sei in Anish Kapoors Skulptur "Cloud Gate" , besser bekannt als "The Bean", eingeschlossen. Wie "Ocula" berichtet, geht der Scherz auf eine satirische Aktivistengruppe zurück, die 2025 mit Protesten die vermeintliche Befreiung des Mannes forderte. Nun wurde die Aktion nach London übertragen: Dort wollten Unbekannte den Marble Arch um sieben Zoll verschieben, um einen Gefangenen zu befreien. Ein Vertreter des Künstlers Stuart Semple, der sich seit Jahren mit Kapoor streitet, wies eine Beteiligung seines Mandanten zurück. Dieser sei am Wochenende zu Hause bei seinem Hund gewesen – ein "wasserdichtes Alibi". Belege für den Mann in der Bohne gibt es natürlich nicht.

Und noch mehr Satire: Die anonyme Künstlergruppe "The Secret Handshake" hat in Washington D.C. erneut eine karikaturistische Trump-Statue aufgestellt. Birgit Rieger stellt im "Tagesspiegel" die Urheber vor; die Gruppe soll aus weniger als fünf Mitgliedern bestehen. Zu ihren früheren Arbeiten gehören eine Statue von Trump und Jeffrey Epstein in "Titanic"-Pose sowie eine goldene Toilettenskulptur als Kommentar zu Trumps Umbau des Weißen Hauses. Die Identität der Beteiligten bleibt geheim; ihre Werke werden meist binnen Stunden entfernt.

Kunstmarkt

In der "Financial Times" berichtet Melanie Gerlis über die erste Frieze Abu Dhabi , die trotz geopolitischer Spannungen vom 19. bis 22. November stattfinden soll. Der Krieg zwischen den USA und Iran verunsichere internationale Besucher, doch Galerien und Institutionen hielten an ihren Plänen fest. Parallel wächst die Kulturszene des Emirats: Das Guggenheim Abu Dhabi soll im Dezember eröffnen , Sotheby's veranstaltet seine erste Auktion vor Ort. Zugleich bleiben Grenzen bestehen: Kritik an der Regierung und am Islam sowie explizit sexuelle Werke seien unerwünscht. Gerlis beschreibt eine Region im kulturellen Aufbruch, dessen langfristige Perspektiven die Akteure optimistisch einschätzten.

article_text:
A total of five films tied for top nominations as the 2026 Gotham Film Awards spread the wealth in a big way Tuesday ahead of its upcoming 38 th ceremony. The NYC event that opens the movie awards season saw All of a Sudden , Clarissa , The Invite , La Gradiva and Tender Loving Care all score four noms each.

Everytime, Josephine, Minotaur, Possible Love, Primetime, Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma and Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother nabbed three nominations apiece.

‘Ink’ Helmer Danny Boyle To Receive Gotham Film Awards’ Director Tribute

2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More

Best Features noms include: Clarissa (Neon) , Club Kid (A24); The Debut (A24); Dreams in Nightmares (Lunette Films) ; The Invite (A24) ; Josephine (Sumerian Pictures) ; Mouse (Independent Film Company) ; Paper Tiger (Neon); Primetime (A24); Teenage Sex And Death At Camp Miasma (Mubi); and Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother (Amazon MGM Studios).

The Gothams expanded its Best Feature category last year.

Watch on Deadline

A24 and Neon dominated this year’s nominations, with, respectively, 15 and 14 apiece. New distributor 1-2 Special had eight noms (for Everytime, La Gradiva and Closure ). Mubi also had eight (for Teenage Sex and Death, Fatherland and Minotaur ). Nominations were spread among 42 features and 25 performances in 11 categories, including the Audience Award, which has reappeared for 2026 after a six-year hiatus.

“It’s a pleasure to announce this year’s nominees. It has been a remarkable year for film, with audiences turning out in theaters for bold, distinctive work from first-time filmmakers and established artists alike,” said Jeffrey Sharp, Executive Director of The Gotham Film & Media Institute. “This year’s nominations, alongside our Tributes and the return of the Audience Award, reflect that abundance and celebrate the creative community that has been at the heart of The Gothams for more than three decades.”

The Gotham Awards aim to elevate independent film and it its nominations and winners often include smaller films and distributors. However, it eliminated a budget cap for eligibility in 2023, opening the door for larger-budget studio fare compete. Previously, budgets couldn’t surpass $35 million.

Netflix’s Possible Love by Lee Joon-dong was nominated for Best International Feature, Best Original Screenplay and Outstanding Lead Performance for Jean Do-yeon. The streamer’s buzzy La Bola Negra along with Possible Love, INK , and Gentle Monster were not eligible for Best Feature under the category’s eligibility rules. T he Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth wasn’t submitted for consideration before the Gothams’ deadline.

La Bola Negra ‘s Guitarricadelafuente was nominated in the Breakthrough Performer category and the film for an Audience Award.

Nominees were selected by committees of film critics, journalists, festival programmers and film curators. Separate juries of writers, directors, actors, producers, editors and other industry professionals will determine the winners.

Returning after a six-year hiatus, the Gotham Audience Award “celebrates films that transcend the screen to become defining cultural moments, capturing audiences’ attention through their impact, reach, and resonance.” The nominees include Backrooms, La Bola Negra, The Drama, The Invite, Michael, Obsession, Project Hail Mary and You Can See Everything.

Gotham members will vote to determine the winner. This year’s nominees were curated from films submitted to The Gothams for consideration, measured by opening-weekend per-theater average against the highest-rated and most-watched films of 2026, as reported in box office tracking and on Letterboxd.

This year’s sprawling announcement was quite a difference from 2025, when Paul Thomas Anderson’s Warner Bros thriller One Battle After Another led all nominations with a record six noms on its way to the Oscar Best Picture.

All winners will be unveiled at an awards ceremony November 30 at Cipriani Wall Street in Lower Manhattan.

Below are the noms by films and distributor, followed by the full list of nominees.

editorial_title_zh: 宛如电影：格雷戈里·克鲁德森摄影展在雷焦艾米利亚举办

Per esempio, lo si scopre dal fatto che i personaggi ritornano di continuo nelle serie, così come i simboli». L’elemento di grande interesse della mostra risiede nella possibilità di osservare l’evoluzione formale e concettuale della ricerca di Crewdson. Ogni suo scatto è una sintesi di fotografia, cinema, pittura, letteratura e psicanalisi. Gregory Crewdson ha rivoluzionato la fotografia contemporanea: le sue opere, che apparentemente sembrano delle fotografie, sono in realtà un assemblaggio di infiniti scatti della scena, dei personaggi che ne fanno parte e degli oggetti presenti."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/alone_street_2018_2019_gregory_crewdson-1024x577.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Alone Street (2018 – 2019) © Gregory Crewdson", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ognuno di questi viene inserito con un lungo e precisissimo lavoro di postproduzione, a comporre una tela che racconta una narrazione ricca di simboli, rimandi alla storia della pittura e alla letteratura. Gli infiniti scatti sono ottenuti allestendo un set cinematografico: una troupe, attori professionisti e abitanti locali coinvolti come interpreti, scenografie costruite e un uso della luce, nebbie e pioggia. Ne nasce un’immagine che è un frame di un film mai stato girato. Una sorta di immagine-mondo, rubando la definizione di libro-mondo, ovvero che racchiude molti racconti e una pluralità di linguaggi."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "La mostra di Gregory Crewdson a Reggio Emilia"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Il primo capitolo della trilogia, Cathedral of the Pines , nasce tra il 2012 e il 2014 a Becket, in Massachusetts, dove Crewdson si era trasferito da New York dopo una dura separazione e una crisi creativa durata tre anni. In questo paese andava da bambino in vacanza e il titolo riprende quello di un sentiero della zona che era solito percorrere. Il curatore racconta come è nata: «Un giorno, Crewdson andò a sciare in mezzo a questa foresta e vide una scritta col nome della località in cui si trovava. Poco dopo, riuscì a visualizzare le 31 foto delle serie ispirandosi a questo nome, che poi sarà quello che userà."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/cathedral_of_the_pines_2014_gregory_crewdson-1024x767.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Cathedral of the Pines, 2014 © Gregory Crewdson", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Un po’ come era successo a David Lynch a cui, mentre era alla guida, è apparso tutto il film Mullholand Drive , che avrebbe realizzato poco dopo. Già in questa serie si rintracciano i temi chiave della grammatica visiva del fotografo americano. Nella foto The mattress , per esempio, ci sono i vuoti che si alternano agli alberi, ma anche gli specchi: riflessi d’acqua e laghi a presentare il tema del doppio, espresso con figure che sembrano interrogarsi sulla propria immagine. «Se ci concentriamo sulla fotografia, vediamo che a destra del soggetto principale ci sono dei passi, ma non sappiamo chi li abbia tracciati. Quando guardiamo le foto di Crewdson abbiamo sempre la sensazione di trovarci in un film che nella realtà non esiste, perché parliamo di fotografia. Non è mai successo nulla, ma noi, come spettatori, spendiamo tempo a ricostruire un ipotetico prima e dopo». Chi guarda è sempre coinvolto nelle stratificazioni di simboli e di significati: se avvicina il naso ai lavori esposti si perde negli infiniti dettagli."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/pickup_truck_2014_gregory_crewdson-1024x766.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pickup Truck (2014) © Gregory Crewdson", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "L’America di Crewdson"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "La provincia americana diventa il luogo di una ricerca sul vuoto esistenziale che attraversa tutte e tre le serie. Il titolo fa riferimento al comportamento delle falene che, quando vengono confuse dalle luci artificiali della città, perdono la direzione. article_text:
Un’America che sembra vera, ma che non esiste. Immobile in un tempo fermo che si racconta nei paesaggi e nelle situazioni astratte ricche di simboli e significati rubati all’arte e alla letteratura. Al centro dei lavori di Gregory Crewdson c’è una provincia desolata, quella postindustriale al sapore di Edward Hopper e delle atmosfere del cinema di David Lynch e di Alfred Hitchcock, con un pizzico di Paris-Texas di Wim Wenders. Curata da Jean-Charles Vergne e realizzata in collaborazione con Gallerie d’Italia di Intesa Sanpaolo, la mostra Gregory Crewdson. Eveningside ai Chiostri di San Pietro a Reggio Emilia, fino al 17 gennaio 2027, riunisce la trilogia fotografica a cui Gregory Crewdson ha lavorato per un decennio, dal 2012 al 2022, che comprende le serie Cathedral of the Pines (2012-2014), An Eclipse of Moths (2018-2019) e la più recente Eveningside (2021–2022) .

«Ad oggi la mostra conta 250.000 visitatori, è una travelling exhibition», spiega il curatore Jean-Charles Vergne. «Ma è sempre diversa a seconda di dove si ferma. Qui a Reggio Emilia vedremo le opere non separate per serie, ma mescolate, per mostrare come siano connesse tra loro. Per esempio, lo si scopre dal fatto che i personaggi ritornano di continuo nelle serie, così come i simboli». L’elemento di grande interesse della mostra risiede nella possibilità di osservare l’evoluzione formale e concettuale della ricerca di Crewdson. Ogni suo scatto è una sintesi di fotografia, cinema, pittura, letteratura e psicanalisi. Gregory Crewdson ha rivoluzionato la fotografia contemporanea: le sue opere, che apparentemente sembrano delle fotografie, sono in realtà un assemblaggio di infiniti scatti della scena, dei personaggi che ne fanno parte e degli oggetti presenti.

Ognuno di questi viene inserito con un lungo e precisissimo lavoro di postproduzione, a comporre una tela che racconta una narrazione ricca di simboli, rimandi alla storia della pittura e alla letteratura. Gli infiniti scatti sono ottenuti allestendo un set cinematografico: una troupe, attori professionisti e abitanti locali coinvolti come interpreti, scenografie costruite e un uso della luce, nebbie e pioggia. Ne nasce un’immagine che è un frame di un film mai stato girato. Una sorta di immagine-mondo, rubando la definizione di libro-mondo, ovvero che racchiude molti racconti e una pluralità di linguaggi.

La mostra di Gregory Crewdson a Reggio Emilia

Il primo capitolo della trilogia, Cathedral of the Pines , nasce tra il 2012 e il 2014 a Becket, in Massachusetts, dove Crewdson si era trasferito da New York dopo una dura separazione e una crisi creativa durata tre anni. In questo paese andava da bambino in vacanza e il titolo riprende quello di un sentiero della zona che era solito percorrere. Il curatore racconta come è nata: «Un giorno, Crewdson andò a sciare in mezzo a questa foresta e vide una scritta col nome della località in cui si trovava. Poco dopo, riuscì a visualizzare le 31 foto delle serie ispirandosi a questo nome, che poi sarà quello che userà.

Un po’ come era successo a David Lynch a cui, mentre era alla guida, è apparso tutto il film Mullholand Drive , che avrebbe realizzato poco dopo. Non è magia: è come se fosse sempre stato tutto lì, come se fosse stato necessario un click per aprire una porta su un universo che era sempre esistito». Già in questa serie si rintracciano i temi chiave della grammatica visiva del fotografo americano. Nella foto The mattress , per esempio, ci sono i vuoti che si alternano agli alberi, ma anche gli specchi: riflessi d’acqua e laghi a presentare il tema del doppio, espresso con figure che sembrano interrogarsi sulla propria immagine. «Se ci concentriamo sulla fotografia, vediamo che a destra del soggetto principale ci sono dei passi, ma non sappiamo chi li abbia tracciati. Quando guardiamo le foto di Crewdson abbiamo sempre la sensazione di trovarci in un film che nella realtà non esiste, perché parliamo di fotografia. Non è mai successo nulla, ma noi, come spettatori, spendiamo tempo a ricostruire un ipotetico prima e dopo». Chi guarda è sempre coinvolto nelle stratificazioni di simboli e di significati: se avvicina il naso ai lavori esposti si perde negli infiniti dettagli.

L’America di Crewdson

La provincia americana diventa il luogo di una ricerca sul vuoto esistenziale che attraversa tutte e tre le serie. È lo stesso senso di attesa che attraversa anche An Eclipse of Moths (Falene) , realizzata tra il 2018 e il 2019 nei territori postindustriali dell’America profonda. Il titolo fa riferimento al comportamento delle falene che, quando vengono confuse dalle luci artificiali della città, perdono la direzione. Una metafora della condizione contemporanea: i suoi personaggi sembrano attratti da luci isolate, incapaci di trovare una direzione.

In Eveningside c’è un’America fatta di strade deserte, vetrine illuminate e figure statiche, dove sembra che qualcosa sia accaduto, generando una immobilità immersa in un silenzio o una situazione di attesa, una sospensione senza certezze. «In Massachusetts non esiste una Eveningside ; essa non sorge da nessuna parte pur essendo ovunque». Le figure che popolano le sue immagini, apparendo sparse e rarefatte, vengono spesso ritratte attraverso le vetrine dei negozi, riflesse nello specchio di un locale o posizionate sotto la cornice apparentemente banale della routine quotidiana. Ponti ferroviari, portoni d’ingresso, portici, la tettoia di uno sportello bancomat, una latteria, un mercato rionale o un negozio di ferramenta. Il tutto, impiegando per la prima volta un unico colore, un bianco e nero con mille sfumature. Anche in questa serie torna il tema del doppio, espresso attraverso lo specchio che diventa tema ricorrente: sia in Madeline’s Beauty Salon e Woman in Bathroom . Ma in Eveningside Tattoo diventa il tramite attraverso cui lo sguardo della persona fotografata incontra chi la osserva, cioè lo spettatore.

Viene spontaneo chiedersi, prima o poi girerà un film? «Prima o poi capiterà. Pare ne avesse parlato addirittura con Cate Blanchett. Ma tutto è misterioso con Crewdson», conclude il curatore. Staremo a vedere.

article_text:
Netflix ‘s theatrical play was bound to have a few hiccups as it works through the kinks of putting movies in theaters for extended runs. One of its big upcoming releases, David Fincher’s “ The Further Mis-adventures of Cliff Booth ” starring Brad Pitt , won’t be playing at some major theater chains when it opens this Thanksgiving.

Regal and Cinemark have declined to play “ Cliff Booth ” on their IMAX screens as part of the film ‘s IMAX-exclusive theatrical run beginning November 25, IndieWire has learned. For now, the film will play only on AMC’s IMAX screens worldwide, plus a few other smaller circuits with IMAX screens, bringing its worldwide screen total to about 550. AMC has about 200 IMAX screens in the U.S., which is the majority, while Regal has about 100 and Cinemark has closer to 20.

Those theaters will likely hold “Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” for a second weekend rather than play a Netflix movie that will be available to stream sooner (it drops on Netflix on December 23, in time for Christmas). Normally, IMAX dictates what titles will play on its screens, and theaters don’t have much of a choice, but in this case, because IMAX came aboard as a partner late in the game, IMAX allowed theater chains to opt out of “Cliff Booth” if they chose and would rather stick with “Hunger Games,” which it looks like they’ll do.

It’s a small letdown for Netflix, but there’s always a fight for premium IMAX screens, and moving “Cliff Booth” to Thanksgiving so it could have this IMAX-exclusive window was a big part of the thinking. Netflix had originally slated Greta Gerwig’s “Narnia” movie there , but it moved into February so that it could have a longer run in theaters and a clearer window at IMAX screens.

This isn’t even the only kerfuffle around screens and streamers that took place this week, as Puck, which originally reported the “Cliff Booth” news, added that Regal, Alamo Drafthouse, and also AMC are all among chains that are opting to not play Amazon’s “Ali G: Who Iz I?” as part of an “extended release” Amazon is planning for the film. That movie opened in just 150 select theaters last weekend as part of a brief theatrical stunt, and it’s dropping on streaming even sooner; though it never reported box office data for it, the Sacha Baron Cohen comedy is intending to continue its run, though the major chains are now opting not to hold it. Amazon did not respond to a request about how many screens the film will play on this weekend.
excerpt_original: David Fincher's film with Brad Pitt has an exclusive IMAX theatrical window beginning on Thanksgiving via AMC's 500 screens worldwide.

article_text:
LYON, France — French distributor Malavida has picked up Wang Chao ’s “A Woman,” the Chinese filmmaker’s 2022 drama that won the screenplay prize at San Sebastián but has never received a theatrical release in France. Malavida is also preparing a wider retrospective of his work for spring 2027.

The acquisitions, announced during Lyon’s International Classic Film Market ( MIFC ), also include three earlier Wang titles — “The Orphan of Anyang” (2001), “Day and Night” (2004) and “Luxury Car” (2006) — with plans to restore “The Orphan of Anyang” and bring the filmmaker to France for the retrospective, scheduled to launch March 24.

Related Stories

‘Helluva Boss’ Actor Lashes Out at NYCC Heckler: ‘I’m Going to Jump Over This Fence and End You’

'Avatar: Seven Havens' Renewed for Seasons 3 and 4 at Paramount+

A separate theatrical release is being considered for “A Woman.”

For Malavida co-founder Anne-Laure Brénéol, the acquisitions are a chance to bring back into view a filmmaker whose work has become harder to see.

“It’s a discovery, an incursion, into China with an extraordinary dissident filmmaker who has somewhat fallen into oblivion because the movies he made during the 2010s weren’t released internationally,” she told Variety. “His last film, even though it won prizes, was never released [outside of China]. It really felt like the right moment to rediscover Wang Chao’s work.”

The company is also adding three Dino Risi titles to its theatrical slate: “The Easy Life” (1962), screened at this year’s Lumière Film Festival , “The Monsters” (1963) and “Tolgo il disturbo” (1990), known in France as “Valse d’amour.” The latter, starring Vittorio Gassman and Elliott Gould, has never been re-released theatrically in France. The three films will form part of a Risi retrospective scheduled for summer 2027.

Malavida is also screening a newly restored 4K digital version of Michael Radford’s “1984” in Lyon as part of the festival’s Lumière Classics program —– its first French theatrical showing since its original 1984 release. The restoration was supervised by Oscar-winning cinematographer Roger Deakins , who shot the original film.

The distributor is also preparing a new French-language version of Soviet animator Fyodor Khitruk’s 1969 “Winnie and His Friends,” narrated and sung by French musician and actor Philippe Katerine . Set for release on Feb. 25, 2027, the program will also be available in a French-subtitled version and has received the backing of French arthouse cinema association AFCAE’s young audiences group.

The collaboration continues a long relationship between Katerine and Malavida, which is celebrating its 20th anniversary. His directorial debut “Peau de cochon” was the first film the company ever released, in 2005, and is now being brought back to theaters.

“At the time, it was very complicated. Philippe wasn’t as known as today. He was just making music and wasn’t the superstar he later became,” Brénéol recalled. “The press was excited about the film, but its theatrical release was not a success. We’re very happy to bring it back for Malavida’s 20th anniversary.”

The film, an unconventional and deeply personal work mixing humor and fantasy, will receive its first DCP release, having originally been distributed on video. Malavida has also previously worked with Katerine on the French-language version of Soviet animated shorts by Eduard Nazarov.

The distributor’s 2027 slate also includes Konrad Wolf’s “I Was Nineteen,” scheduled for April 21. Malavida discovered the East German filmmaker’s 1968 feature during a retrospective at last year’s Lumière Festival, an encounter Brénéol described as an extraordinarily powerful emotional experience, and subsequently acquired it for French distribution.

Another rediscovery is Jean-Henri Meunier’s 1979 “La Bande du Rex,” a rock-infused film starring French singer Jacques Higelin as Franckie Mégalo, a rebellious film projectionist. Featuring an original soundtrack composed by Higelin, the film is scheduled for re-release in May.

The MIFC runs alongside Lyon’s Lumière Film Festival until Oct. 16.

article_text:
The Artnet Bulletin is our daily digest of five items from around the art world that are worth knowing. A different writer takes over each morning.

A Papal Audience

Pope Leo XIV continues his campaign to champion and protect art. On Saturday, the pontiff welcomed the Bizot Group , the international network of directors from the world’s largest museums, to the Vatican for an audience. Speaking on the meeting’s theme of “materiality,” he described matter as a gift entrusted to human care, shaped by artists into expressions of transcendent meaning, and as a form of memory that museums carry across generations. He closed by praising the group, currently led by the Rijksmuseum ‘s director, Taco Dibbits , for safeguarding heritage that “belongs to all humanity,” according to a transcript of his remarks. The meeting came just days after the pontiff announced plans to bolster the church’s alliance with artists and cultural institutions, citing rising threats of censorship and homogenization posed by A.I.

Pope Leo XIV meets with directors of museums around the world during an audience at the Apostolic Palace on October 10, 2026 in Vatican City, Vatican. Photo: Simone Risoluti – Vatican Media via Vatican Pool/ Getty Images.

More Kennedy Center Developments

It’s impossible to guess what could happen next with the Trump-run Kennedy Center . The embattled arts complex, currently closed to the public, has appointed a new artistic director, according to NPR , Rick Canny has been serving as a consultant to the center since April 2025, through his talent-management firm Favor the Artist , during which time staff have lodged complaints about his business practices. His previous clients have included ZZ Top , Whitesnake , and Tommy Lee .

Meanwhile, the Financial Times reported that Gaurav Srivastava , a major donor to the center, was a secret FBI informant from 2019 to 2024. Unsealed court documents show that the bureau had flagged concerns about his “reliability and honesty.” The disclosure emerges from a lawsuit by sanctioned Dutch oil trader Niels Troost, who accuses Srivastava of defrauding him of more than $43 million, an allegation that Srivastava denies.

Brotherly Love

Tondo of the Two Brothers (Antinoopolis Tondo), second century. Courtesy of the Egyptian Museum.

Egypt unveiled a restored Tondo of the Two Brothers , a prized second-century Fayoum portrait. Specialists from Rome and conservators from the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir spent three weeks patching up the work, according to the Associated Press . Notable for its circular shape and double subject, the wax-based painting had suffered termite damage to its wooden support, and restorers recovered the features of the brother on the right. Egypt will lend a major part of the Fayoum collection to a Rome exhibition running from November 2026 to May 2027, marking the first time the work will travel abroad.

Backlash Over Smashed Porcelain

The British Museum is facing criticism after a Qing dynasty porcelain bowl and a ceramic box from the Sir Percival David Collection were smashed on October 4, provoking anger in Chinese national media and on social media. The bowl fell from its mount in a display cabinet in Room 95 and landed on the box below. Staff who reviewed CCTV can’t explain why: The mount was undamaged and the room was empty. A museum spokesperson told the South China Morning Post that the objects are already with the conservation team for repair.

Frieze Week Potpourri

Happy Frieze Week, London!

Among the countless gallery openings, one I wasn’t counting on: Harry Blain , formerly of Blain Southern , which shuttered abruptly in 2020 and allegedly left many of its artists financially in the lurch, is hosting a private view today at 23 Bruton Street for his new venture, Blain . The show, titled “The Best Way Out Is Always Through,” features works by Felix Gonzalez-Torres and Bruce Nauman. If you want to see Gagosian ’s blockbuster Magritte show , “This Is Still Not a Pipe,” leave extra time: When I went on Saturday, the line to get in snaked around the corner and down Mount Street. (I admit I used my press credentials to skip it.) It simply wouldn’t be Frieze without a big ol’ dino from David Aaron , which is bringing a remarkably complete 150-million-year-old Camarasaurus supremus skull to Frieze Masters. article_text:
Solving a mystery that has puzzled experts for centuries, scientists at the University of Sheffield in England have recreated the color-changing properties of the British Museum ’s storied 1,600-year-old Lycurgus Cup, which is green in typical lighting but turns red when lit from behind.

“To me, it’s magic,” Lisa Hollands, a technician who worked on project, told the Guardian . She added that “people have tried it before with limited success” and called the undertaking a “labor of love.”

The Roman cup, which was named one of the seven glass wonders of the world by the organizing committee behind the UN-designated International Year of Glass in 2022, bears a design that alludes to King Lycurgus from the sixth book of Homer’s Iliad . The design celebrates the triumph of Dionysus, the god of wine, over a vine-wrapped Lycurgus.

In their attempt to emulate the chameleonic quality of the vessel, the researchers embedded nanoparticles of gold and silver into glass—“each a thousand times smaller than a grain of sand,” as the Guardian described them.

Of the process, Hollands said, “So, for this glass, if light is shone through it, the gold and silver particles block blue and green light, only allowing reds and oranges to pass through. If light is reflected off the surface, the particles have the effect of scattering the light, giving the opaque green color we see.”

She also confessed: “If the Romans could have seen me experimenting, they’d probably laugh and ask: ‘Why does she not know how to make this?’”

A related sculpture by the glass artist Elliot Walker commissioned by the University of Sheffield will feature in the school’s Festival of the Mind in November before entering the collection of its Turner Museum of Glass.

Ian Freestone, emeritus professor of archaeological materials at University College London, suggested the green-to-red color change could relate to the ripening of a grape. “The depicted scene has grape vines pulling Lycurgus into the underworld,” he said. “So it could have been used in a drinking ceremony of some sort.”

article_text:
One of Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos ‘ guiding principles that he has frequently discussed is Netflix’s ability to adapt, change, and evolve. He introduced ads when it looked like there would never be, he never wanted to do sports or live events until he warmed to them, and we’re finally seeing Netflix soften on theatrical . In fact, it was Sarandos’ vision along with co-founder Reed Hastings to move away from the DVD mailing business that was Netflix’s cash cow and make a push toward the streaming model that would disrupt Hollywood.

In an interview with CNBC from January , Sarandos discussed creating a working environment where “there are no sacred cows here.”

“It’s a great way to position yourself as a curious thinker inside of our business is if you challenge conventional wisdom, because I think Netflix was built on challenging conventional wisdom on almost everything,” he said.

In the past week, Sarandos has demonstrated there truly are no sacred cows at Netflix. Roughly 1,000 staffers were let go, and both chief content officer Bela Bajaria and film chief Dan Lin were shown the door. Taking Bajaria’s place is Peter Rice, a well-liked former Disney and Fox executive, and rumors abound about who could step into Lin’s shoes and how the film team will be reshaped.

The exit of two of Sarandos’ major lieutenants on the creative side of the business leaves little additional room for blame and all eyes on him to set things right. There’s no one left to fire. If Netflix’s stock price — now below $70 after being above $120 a year ago — continues to slide, if some of Netflix’s engagement numbers continue to struggle, if growth for Netflix is not where he would like it to be , all on the eve of the company’s earnings on Tuesday, October 20, it’s not a stretch to imagine that he might be feeling some heat too.

Sarandos, though, has been in this position before, and Netflix has continued to come out on top. First it was Qwikster. In 2011, Netflix had the idea to spin off its streaming and DVD business into two separate companies and label the DVD mailers under a new company name. The decision was so unpopular that then-CEO Hastings reversed it within a month , and stock prices promptly went back up. It took 25 years, but DVDs were finally sunsetted at Netflix in April 2023.

Then came what was known as the “Netflix Correction.” Netflix in April 2022 experienced its first-ever quarter in which it reported a loss of subscribers , roughly 200,000 that quarter. It would lose nearly another 1 million a quarter later. Wall Street panicked, and Sarandos jumped into gear. Among the major changes Netflix made, it started an aggressive crackdown on password sharing, estimating an enormous number of families and households were using someone else’s account to watch Netflix. And to win back those people who were booted off, it rapidly launched a more affordable ad-supported tier for those who didn’t want to pay full freight. Over time, Netflix grew to well over 300 million subscribers to the point that it doesn’t even report how many subscribers it adds each quarter now.

How Netflix got into this predicament is a different story. Wall Street didn’t love when Netflix wanted to buy Warner Bros. Discovery’s film business, and the stock didn’t exactly bounce back when it lost it to Paramount, even with a few billion dollars infused into the business as a kill fee. Since then, Netflix has aggressively ramped up podcasts in an effort to get people to start watching their favorites on Netflix, not YouTube, signing deals with Spotify, Barstool Sports, iHeartMedia, and Jay Shetty’s “On Purpose” all within the last 12 months.

It also used some of that Paramount money to splurge on another NFL package, rights to stream the World Cup internationally, and even a few marquee MLB games. Some of the other creative content choices of late have included releasing a 30-minute gameplay trailer for the highly anticipated video game “Grand Theft Auto VI,” which is the sort of thing that usually gets attention on X and Twitch rather than Netflix. Netflix not long ago retooled some of its Kids and Family content, picking up streaming rights to “Sesame Street” and “Ms. Rachel” while dumping “CoComelon,” and the streamer is planning a “Sesame Street” film as well. Netflix is also finally making the bet that heavy marketing spending on some movies in theaters might make a difference for its titles on streaming down the road.

That’s how Sarandos is tackling the engagement problem, but some analysts are bullish that Netflix’s ad business is what will lead it back to the promised land. Wedbush late last week wrote in its report that the engagement changes are going to take some time, even longer with all the staff upheaval. But ad revenue, Wedbush writes, is “on track to double to roughly $3 billion in 2026” and gave it a 12-month stock price target of $90.

In all this time, Netflix and Sarandos are still chasing a Best Picture Oscar that has eluded them, and “La Bola Negra” may be its best shot yet . Wall Street will still have its own concerns regardless of awards, but momentum like that would be a symbolic victory for Sarandos and Netflix as it navigates this latest period of turbulence. The now-departed Lin would deserve some credit for the win if it were to happen, but Sarandos would be able to take a victory lap as much as any. It would be a sign that the Old Guard of Hollywood has softened its stance on Netflix , that its movies for grown-ups (not just “KPop Demon Hunters”) can capture the zeitgeist, and that Sarandos still has some levers to pull to show Netflix can still change, be disruptive, and an industry leader.

But if none of the levers he’s pulled so far work out, have you thought about a DVD business?

article_text:
Films and events

Dare

Atlantic Rhapsody

Da Xi Yang

A young man embarks on a surreal quest to find his long-lost father in a remarkable feature debut that spans 20 years of recent Chinese history.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Zhong Kaifeng

Screenwriters Zhong Kaifeng, Wu Linfeng

With Yin Fang, Wang Yitong, Li Xueqin

China 2026. 101min

Courtesy of Rediance

Languages Mandarin Chinese, Japanese With English subtitles

Introduction

Opening with the unfortunate fate of a shark, which haunts the main character in unique ways, oceans – both physically and metaphorically – play an outsized role in this absurdist father-son drama. Zhong Kaifeng’s ambitious, award-winning film sees its complex sound design play a heightened role, as time and space collapse and blur.

Sergio Fant

Content advice

Contains scenes of animal slaughter and graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Hearing

Known for his precise and enigmatic filmmaking, here Lê Bảo crafts a meditative anti-love story revealing fragile connections between humans, sounds and unseen worlds.

Moonglow

The queen of sensual cinema returns with a 1970s Manila-set neo-noir about a police officer-turned-criminal under investigation by her former lover.

French Girls

Effortlessly moving from one moment to the next, Hyun Lee’s fashionably hip and charming micro-budget debut heralds an exciting directorial talent.

article_text:
Films and events

Documentary Competition

Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing

Erik Shirai’s beautifully shot and fascinating film grants rare access inside the disciplined inner domain of Japan’s sumo wrestling world.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Erik Shirai

Japan-USA-UK-Denmark 2026. 99min

Courtesy of ESPN Films

Languages Japanese, Mongolian With English subtitles

Introduction

In pop culture, sumo wrestling isn’t always treated with the seriousness it deserves. But in this gripping film, Shirai repositions it as an ancient sport whose competitors are forced to submit to gruelling training. Unfolding over the course of a year, Sumo follows a number of fighters, highlighting their dedication and the sacrifices they make in order to be the very best.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Look Back

Spanning more than a decade, Hirokazu Koreeda’s tender coming-of-age story follows two girls who bond over their passion for and dream of becoming manga artists.

Godzilla Minus Zero

The sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s acclaimed 2023 film is a true cinematic spectacle that’s sure to grip fans of Godzilla, as well as newcomers to the franchise.

The Match

Few sporting contests loom as large in the public imagination as the dramatic 1986 World Cup Quarter Final between England and Argentina, as this documentary details.

article_text:
王子さまが暮らす小さな星へ

『星の王子さま』のフランス刊行80周年を記念した特別イベント 「フランス刊行80周年記念『星の王子さま 大切なものを探しに空の旅へ』」 が 六本木ヒルズ 東京シティビュー で開幕した。会期は11月13日から2027年2月14日まで。

『星の王子さま』は、フランスの飛行士であり作家の、 アントワーヌ・ド・サン＝テグジュペリ の代表作。語り手の飛行士が、飛行機の故障で不時着したサハラ砂漠で不思議な星から来た小さな王子さまと出会い、絆を結び、別れるまでの10日間と、そのあいだに飛行士が聞き知った王子さまの旅路の物語を描く。1943年にアメリカで初版が刊行され、46年にはサン＝テグジュペリの母国フランスで出版された。2026年はフランスでの出版から80周年となる。

本展は全5章の構成。第1章「小さな星に住んでいる王子さま」では、東京の空と街を背景に、『星の王子さま』の世界観が広がる。惑星に立つ王子さまのオブジェの奥には、6つの惑星に暮らす個性豊かな住人たちのバナーが垂れ下がり、イルミネーションが輝く。物語に登場する小さな惑星とその住人たちが、空に浮かぶように配置された空間は、王子さまの旅の始まりを思わせる。

惑星に立つ王子さまの作品の横には、この物語の重要なメッセージである「l'essentiel（レソンシエル）＝本当に大切なもの」にまつわるキツネのセリフが掲げられている。王子さまと星の住人たち、そしてキツネとの交流を通して語られる言葉には、目に見えるものだけでは測れない価値が込められている。いまを生きる私たちにも、大切なものを見つめ直すきっかけを与えてくれる。

飛行士サン＝テグジュペリが紡いだ物語

第2章「作家アントワーヌ・ド・サン＝テグジュペリの生涯」では、北西アフリカ、南大西洋、南米を結ぶ航空路の開拓者であり、夜間飛行の先駆者のひとりでもあったサン＝テグジュペリの生涯を、年表と写真資料を通してたどる。

フランス航空史に名を残す飛行士でありながら、なぜ作家として『星の王子さま』を執筆するに至ったのか。空を飛びたいという夢を叶えるまでの過程から、『星の王子さま』を生み出すきっかけにもなった遭難などの危険な経験の数々、そして作家としての歩みを、当時の時代背景とともに読み解くことができる。

第3章「名作『星の王子さま』の誕生」では、貴重なドローイング41点を原画に忠実に再現した複製画が展示される。『星の王子さま』に登場する個性豊かなキャラクターや印象的なモチーフは、サン＝テグジュペリ自身の人生や経験、実際に出会った人々や動物などが元になっているといわれている。ドローイングを通して、物語の登場人物やモチーフが生まれた背景に思いを巡らせることができる。

章の入り口には、うわばみ（大蛇）がゾウを飲み込んだ様子を表現した半立体作品が登場する。語り手の飛行士「ぼく」が子供の頃、うわばみがゾウを飲み込んだ様子を描いた絵を、大人たちはただの「帽子」だと勘違いしてしまう。目に見えるかたちだけで物事を判断し、その奥にある本質を見落としてしまう大人たちを描いた、物語の冒頭を飾る象徴的なエピソードだ。パネルの裏表を用いてその絵を表現した作品からも、「目に見えない大切なもの」という物語のメッセージが伝わってくる。

世界中で愛される物語、その先にあるもの

アメリカでの初版刊行以来、680以上の言語・方言に翻訳され、世界累計発行部数は3億部を超える『星の王子さま』。第4章「世界中で愛され続ける『星の王子さま』」では、世界各国で出版された70冊の書籍の表紙が並ぶ。同じ物語でありながら、国や言語によって異なる装丁やイラストの表現を見比べられるのも興味深い。

第5章「大切なものを探しに」では、物語の名場面が飛び出す絵本のようなインスタレーションになって展示されている。ページをめくるように場面をたどりながら、王子さまの旅路を追体験できる空間だ。世界中でいまなお愛されている物語に触れながら、自分にとって本当に大切なものは何か、あらためて考えてみてはいかがだろう。
